items.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Commandante Almay, that was his name. He loved to compose the little songs like that, and I recorded some of his pieces, and then he liberated me from the army in six month.

ctx.x: Almost three years, two years and a half. It was supposed to be three years, but I get rid of it because of the integration of the commander who liked to compose music. The
Commandante Almay, that was his name. He loved to compose the little songs like that, and I recorded some of his pieces, and then he liberated me from the army in six month.
So, you were in the army until you were about 18 years old?
